anomalies.observed: The ATtiny45 U2 and ATtiny13 U3 have their corresponding signal pins tied together, including both PB1 pins on PWM and both reset pins on RST. Their other corresponding interface pins are also shared.
anomalies.expected: A fan controller described as ATtiny-driven should use one active MCU, or provide a selection/isolation arrangement so two MCUs cannot drive shared signals simultaneously.

evidence.quote: PWM : J4.1(MISO,passive) R2.1(passive) R5.2(passive) U2.6(PB1,bidirectional) U3.6(PB1,bidirectional)
RST : J1.4(Pin_4,passive) J4.5(~{RST},passive) R3.2(passive) U2.1(~{RESET}/PB5,bidirectional) U3.1(~{RESET}/PB5,bidirectional)

anomalies.impact: If both MCUs are populated and enabled, their PB1 outputs can contend on PWM, causing unreliable fan control or stressing the output drivers. Shared reset and programming lines also prevent independent operation.

anomalies.observed: C2 is only 100pF and is the sole capacitor shown from the LM1117-5.0 output rail to ground.
anomalies.expected: The LM1117 output should have an appropriately sized output capacitor; typical LM1117 applications require capacitance on the order of 10µF for stable regulation, rather than 100pF.
anomalies.impact: Insufficient output capacitance can make the regulator unstable or poorly respond to load transients, potentially disturbing the +5V rail and the MCU supply.

parsed.summary: The netlist ties two separate MCU outputs and their control/programming pins together without a selection mechanism, creating a credible contention risk. The LM1117 output also appears to have only a 100pF capacitor, far below typical output-capacitance requirements.
